Monthly payment formula:
\[
PMT=\frac{P(r)}{1-(1+r)^{-n}},\quad r=\frac{APR}{12}
\]
Total cost = \(PMT \times n - \$50{,}000 +\) fee.

**Loan A:** \(r=0.079/12=0.0065833,\ n=60\)  
\(PMT\approx \$1{,}011.43\); total paid \(\approx \$60{,}685.71\)  
Interest \(\approx \$10{,}685.71\); fee \(=2\%\times \$50{,}000=\$1{,}000\)  
Total cost \(\approx \$11{,}685.71\)

**Loan B:** \(r=0.069/12=0.00575,\ n=60\)  
\(PMT\approx \$987.70\); total paid \(\approx \$59{,}262.16\)  
Interest \(\approx \$9{,}262.16\); fee \(=\$0\)  
Total cost \(\approx \$9{,}262.16\)

**Loan C:** \(r=0.059/12=0.0049167,\ n=48\)  
\(PMT\approx \$1{,}171.96\); total paid \(\approx \$56{,}254.10\)  
Interest \(\approx \$6{,}254.10\); fee \(=\$0\)  
Total cost \(\approx \$6{,}254.10\)

Loan C has the lowest total cost.
